<!-- Template: the spine of the guide. The chapter list below is the starter set, not the guide's own: add, remove and rename the includes to match the chapters the guide really has, then delete this line. -->

<!--
  This file is the spine of the guide. Chapters live in _chapters/ and are
  pulled in below; the leading underscore keeps Quarto from also rendering
  each one as a standalone document.

  Build:  quarto render docs/user-guide.qmd
  Output: docs/_output/user-guide.pdf

  The `subtitle` above is overridden by the build, e.g.
    quarto render docs/user-guide.qmd -M "subtitle=Version 1.2.3"
  so a printed page says which build it documents. It reads "Unversioned" only
  when rendered by hand.
-->

{{< pagebreak >}}

<!--
  List of Tables. The substance of a guide is its reference tables, so this is a
  real lookup index rather than front matter.

  Built by hand because `lot: true` does nothing here: Quarto's format reference
  lists the option, but the Typst writer never emits the second outline. Quarto
  does tag every captioned table as a float of kind "quarto-float-tbl", so
  selecting on that gives the same result.

  Only captioned tables appear. Every reference table carries a caption; short
  inline enumerations are left uncaptioned deliberately so they do not dilute
  the list. An uncaptioned lookup table is invisible here, which is the whole
  point of the index - check-guide.ts fails the guide when a table has no caption.
-->
```{=typst}
#outline(
  title: [List of Tables],
  target: figure.where(kind: "quarto-float-tbl"),
)
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

<!--
  Page furniture for the body. Placed after the front matter so the title page,
  the Contents and the List of Tables all stay clean, and so this `set page`
  rule lands on a page boundary rather than forcing a blank page of its own.

  The version reaches the header through the `meta` shortcode, reading the same
  `subtitle` the build overrides with -M.
-->
```{=typst}
#set page(
  header: [
    #set text(8pt, fill: luma(40%))
    [[APP_NAME]] User Guide --- {{< meta subtitle >}}
    #h(1fr)
  ],
)
```

<!--
  Let a long table run onto the next page. Quarto wraps every captioned table in
  `#figure([#table(...)])`, and a Typst figure lays its body out in a block that
  cannot break -- so a table taller than the text area does not paginate. It runs
  past the bottom margin and every remaining row is painted on top of the last one.
  The rows are still in the PDF; they are just stacked into one illegible line.

  Scoped to the table kind on purpose. A bare `#show figure:` would also let a
  screenshot split across a page boundary, which is not wanted -- an image figure
  always fits, so it has nothing to gain and a caption to lose.
-->
```{=typst}
#show figure.where(kind: "quarto-float-tbl"): set block(breakable: true)
```

<!--
  The appendices are titled "Appendix: ..." but section-numbering above would
  otherwise number them as the next chapters. Reset the heading counter and
  switch to letters so they read A, B, C.

  Quarto emits cross-references as native `#ref()`, so @sec-terms and friends
  pick the new letters up on their own - no reference needs editing.
-->
```{=typst}
#counter(heading).update(0)
#set heading(numbering: "A.1")
```
